source.author: verg
source.text: Si mihi non animo fixum immotumque sederet, ne cui me vinclo vellem sociare iugali, postquam primus amor deceptam morte fefellit; si non pertaesum thalami taedaeque fuisset, huic uni forsan potui succumbere culpae.
source.text_original: Si mihi non animo fixum immotumque sederet, / ne cui me vinclo vellem sociare iugali, / postquam primus amor deceptam morte fefellit; / si non pertaesum thalami taedaeque fuisset, / huic uni forsan potui succumbere culpae.
source.text_english: If it were not fixed and unshaken in my mind not to wish to join myself to anyone in the marriage bond, since my first love deceived me and failed me by death, if I had not grown weary of the bridal chamber and the marriage torch, I might perhaps have yielded to this one fault alone.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: nee vellera tantum indignanda manent propiorque ex virgine rapta ille dolor, sed nulla magis sententia menti fixa meae: veniet Phrygia nam pastor ab Ida, qui gemitus irasque pares et mutua Grais dona ferat.
reuse.text_original: nee vellera tantum / indignanda manent propiorque ex virgine rapta / ille dolor, sed nulla magis sententia menti / fixa meae: veniet Phrygia nam pastor ab Ida, / qui gemitus irasque pares et mutua Grais / dona ferat.
reuse.text_english: Not only do the fleeces remain deserving of indignation, and that pain, closer to me, from the virgin who was ravished; but no thought is more firmly fixed in my mind: for the shepherd will come from Phrygian Ida, who will bring to the Greeks groans and wrath in equal measure, and gifts in return.
